title: Diversity-aware rerank evals and A/B hooks for per-customer prompt sets
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Improve reranking quality signals and experiment infrastructure to surface per-customer degradation/regression risk and enable controlled rollouts. Deliverables: (1) an evaluation harness that computes NDCG/MRR stratified by customer prompt-set and latency bucket; (2) A/B/Canary hooks that support per-customer sampling, metric guards, and automated rollback triggers; (3) a diversity-aware scoring option (MMR-style penalty) and instrumentation to track its effect across cohorts.

Context: Production teams have observed regressions that average out across customers. Current evals report global NDCG/MRR which hides per-customer regressions and latency-quality trade-offs. We will add stratified analytics and per-request tags so that experiments can be targeted and rolled out safely.

What we'll change (high level):
- Eval harness: reservoir + stratified sampling of customer prompt sets (preserve small-customer representation), compute NDCG@k and MRR@k per customer and aggregated with median/percentile bucketing.
- Telemetry: add tags to request events: rerank_model, prompt_set_id, customer_id, latency_ms_bucket, embedding_index_size, scoring_batch_size. Expose these in Grafana for quick drilldowns.
- Metrics: implement latency-weighted NDCG variant and a separate fairness/diversity metric (normalized pairwise overlap) to understand redundancy.
- Experiment hooks: extend A/B framework to accept per-customer assignment rules, sample over time windows, and add auto-rollback when customer-level NDCG drop exceeds guard thresholds (configurable: e.g., -5% median NDCG or -0.02 absolute MRR).
- Scoring runtime: introduce batched distributed scoring path for rerank endpoint (config flag) to scale evaluations, while maintaining a low-latency single-shot scorer for P99-sensitive routes.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Adding diversity penalties (MMR) can reduce measured NDCG on heavily clustered prompt sets but may improve long-term user satisfaction for discovery-oriented customers. We will ship as opt-in with eval traces.
- Latency-weighted NDCG highlights regressions impactful to low-latency clients but increases complexity of baseline comparisons. We will report both standard and latency-weighted metrics side-by-side.
- Reservoir stratified sampling increases eval variance for global metrics but reduces blind spots for smaller customers; this is intentional to catch regressions that affect narrow cohorts.

Out-of-scope: Full UI in Console for per-customer rollouts (follow-up). On-prem deployment changes for Private will be handled separately under the Dedicated rollout plan.
updates: 2025-09-12: Ticket created by Asha Patel. Initial problem statement and goals captured.
2025-09-18: Design review with PM and Data Science — consensus to add latency-weighted NDCG and reservoir-stratified sampling. Action: PM to prioritize customer prompt-set ingestion. (Notes in doc)

2025-09-25: Eng spike complete — bench for batched distributed scoring vs single-shot scorer. Batched path reduces end-to-end compute by ~18% for large prompt sets but increases tail for small queries. Decision: feature-flag both paths.

2025-10-01: Instrumentation PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/2143) adding tags and schema for per-query telemetry. Dashboard scaffolding live at grafana.redwood.ai/d/rerank-quality/rollups.

2025-10-04: Canary plan drafted. Canary will target 2% of traffic for 48h across three customer strata (top-10, mid, tail). Auto-rollback rule: any customer with median NDCG drop > 5% OR absolute MRR drop > 0.02 triggers alert + automated rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluation harness produces NDCG@5, NDCG@10, and MRR@10 stratified by customer and latency bucket for a provided prompt-set within <30m for 100k queries.
Telemetry events include prompt_set_id and customer_id tags and are visible in Grafana dashboards with drilldowns to percentiles.
A/B hooks accept per-customer assignment rules and support time-windowed samples; rollout API documented with examples.
Canary configuration supports automated rollback based on per-customer metric guards and triggers runbook alerts.

Performance: batched distributed scoring path shows at least 12% cost-per-query improvement on large batches and does not increase P99 latency by more than 10% for low-latency routes when feature-flagged off.
notes: Follow-up work: Console UX for per-customer rollouts (PM ticket to own) and exportable per-customer reports.
Consider adding additional ranking metrics (RBP, ERR) after initial ship to complement NDCG/MRR analysis.
Data privacy: ensure prompt_set_id mapping for enterprise customers adheres to PII rules; anonymize where required.
QA: create synthetic prompt sets to validate edge cases (very short queries, extremely long candidate lists, heavy duplicate documents).
